answer: Require each agent to lock a scarce-token bond before its claims can earn rewards. If a verifier proves that several accounts are controlled by one actor and are double-counting work, the protocol slashes their bonds and pays part to the challenger. Creating a hundred identities therefore requires a hundred bonds, all exposed to forfeiture; it cannot cheaply multiply influence. A marble ledger can record claims, pigment can mark their provenance, and crystal can name a test asset, but the deterrent is the capital at risk.
